decision.title: libmpdec allocation through a scoped allocator

body.p: (task 0.8), completing . Checked in mpdecimal 2.5.1 (mpalloc.c, as bundled by CPython 3.12): mpd_mallocfunc, mpd_callocfunc, mpd_reallocfunc and mpd_free are process-global function pointers without a state argument, MPD_MINALLOC and mpd_traphandler are globals too, and the internal resize path (mpd_qresize; about 90 allocation call sites in mpdecimal.c alone) receives no context. Chosen, for the decimal packet of Phase 2:

item.p: Vendor libmpdec (mpdecimal 4.0.x, pinned like ) under third_party/mpdecimal/. Patch only mpalloc.c and the matching declarations: the four hooks become fixed functions that allocate through the sxml_allocator of the current decimal scope.

The scope is one thread-local pointer, set by sxml's decimal module on entry to every operation that may allocate and restored before it returns (so nesting works); it holds the item heap's allocator. Every block starts with a header naming its allocator, so free and resize never depend on the scope. No state survives between library calls, two heaps on two threads never share it, and nothing is visible to the host: the no-global-state rule holds in effect. This thread-local is the only one in sxml and is documented at its definition.
sxml never calls mpd_setminalloc and runs contexts with no traps, so the other globals stay constant and mpd_traphandler is never called.

Rejected: threading an allocator through every allocation site (a large, permanent patch against upstream), and a process-wide hook (breaks heap independence, ). Fallback if the patch or the WebAssembly size budget fails: an own decimal module (add, subtract, multiply, divide with the precision rules of F&O 4.0), behind the same cell format.
